content.text:
The bug is fixed. `tomli.loads('s = "caf\\u00e9"')` now returns `{'s': 'café'}`.

**Cause:** In `src/tomli/_parser.py`, `parse_hex_char` advanced `pos` to the *last* hex digit and returned that. `parse_basic_str` then resumed copying from that position, so the last digit appeared twice. `\u00e9` produced `é` followed by a repeated `9`. The same happened to `\U`, `\x`, and any other hex escape.

**Fix:** `parse_hex_char` now returns the position just after the hex digits. I also kept the error location for out-of-range scalar values unchanged, so error messages still point where they did before.

**Regression test:** Added `test_unicode_escape_does_not_repeat_last_digit` to `tests/test_misc.py`. It covers `\u00e9`, `\U0001F600`, `\x41`, and an escape in the middle of a string. I did not change or remove any existing tests.

**Results:** Before the fix, the full suite had 14 failures and 1 skip. After the fix, it runs 19 tests with all passing and 1 skip. That includes the `duplicate-keys` cases, which were failing too and appear to have had the same root cause. I didn't investigate that link in detail.

I haven't committed anything. Tell me if you want a commit with the Co-Authored-By line.
